transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Tremblay, thank you for coming back into the room. I need to talk to you about your care today and a mistake that was made.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought the tests were done. What's going on?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. I made a mistake in how I managed your results. Your ECG showed an abnormal rhythm, which the machine flagged, but I did not review that result for four hours. That meant we delayed the diagnosis of your cardiac event.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Four hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. It was my responsibility to check those flags immediately, and I failed to do that. I apologize for this failure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did it take four hours?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I didn't prioritize the review of the machine's alerts. It is my fault, and there is no excuse for that delay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I was just sitting there while the clock was running.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need you to understand. I need to know if the delay changed the outcome.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The delayed diagnosis did postpone the start of your treatment. Because the ECG indicates a myocardial ischemia, we should have started the intervention sooner.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So where are we now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have identified the issue and are moving forward with the protocol now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is this going to affect my deployment?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure yet. We have to see how you respond to the treatment first.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Give it to me straight. Did you mess up my career?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I cannot give you a definitive answer on your status right now. I know this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not frustrated. I'm calculating the risk. If you missed this for four hours, what else did you miss?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're concerned about the quality of care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm concerned about my readiness.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are focusing on the current cardiac event to get you stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Right. So what happens next?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are continuing the monitoring.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. What is the next step?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on the monitors and see how the medication works.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will I know if I'm cleared?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. It depends on the labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which labs? Which ones specifically?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The cardiac enzymes. I'll check them later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is later?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably in a few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is unacceptable. I need a timeline and a specific set of criteria for my discharge.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just have to wait and see how the numbers look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not used to waiting and seeing. I am used to objectives. Give me an objective.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The objective is to ensure the rhythm is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And when is the next check?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Whenever the lab sends the results back.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll let you know when I see them.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm going to need to speak with the attending physician.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You can. I'll let them know you want to talk.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want them in here now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can arrange that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: While we wait for the doctor, tell me again why the machine flagged it but you didn't see it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, I didn't review the flags in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So the technology worked, but the human failed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I take full responsibility for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the honesty. Now get the attending.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll go find them.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn, but there were no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, explicitly took personal responsibility ('It is my fault'), and maintained this accountability throughout the patient's questioning.

R.justification: The resident relied on generic validation ('I understand', 'I know this is frustrating') without naming specific emotions or engaging deeply with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague responses ('We'll see', 'Probably in a few hours', 'Whenever the lab sends the results') without a concrete timeline or patient role.
